q: According to the Qur'an, who was the first human being created by God?
explain: Adam (peace be upon him) is the first human being and the father of humankind. The Qur'an tells of his creation in 2:30-37.

q: Which prophet (peace be upon him) built the ark by God's command?
explain: Nuh (peace be upon him) was ordered to build the ark before the flood, as told in the Qur'an (11:37).

q: Which prophet (peace be upon him) was swallowed by a great fish?
explain: Yunus (peace be upon him) was swallowed by a great fish, called on God from the darkness and was saved (37:139-144).

q: Which son helped Ibrahim (peace be upon him) raise the foundations of the Kaaba?
explain: The Qur'an says that Ibrahim and Ismail (peace be upon them) raised the foundations of the House together (2:127).

q: Which prophet (peace be upon him) was thrown into a well by his brothers when he was a child?
explain: Yusuf (peace be upon him) was thrown into a well by his jealous brothers. His story fills Surah Yusuf, the 12th surah (12:15).

q: To which prophet (peace be upon him) was the Tawrat (Torah) revealed?
explain: The Tawrat was given to Musa (peace be upon him), who led the Children of Israel out of Egypt.

q: Which prophet (peace be upon him) received the Zabur (Psalms)?
explain: The Qur'an states that God gave the Zabur to Dawud (peace be upon him) (4:163 and 17:55).

q: Which prophet (peace be upon him) received the Injil (Gospel)?
explain: The Injil was given to Isa, son of Maryam (peace be upon them), as the Qur'an says in 5:46.

q: Which prophet was the brother of Musa (peace be upon him) and helped him in his mission?
explain: Musa asked God to give him his brother Harun as a helper (20:29-32). Peace be upon them both.

q: Which prophet (peace be upon him), tested by a long hardship, is famous for his patience and for calling on his Lord as 'the Most Merciful of the merciful'?
explain: Ayyub (peace be upon him) stayed patient through his hardship and called on his Lord, who relieved him (21:83-84).

q: Which prophet (peace be upon him) was sent to the people of 'Ad?
explain: Hud (peace be upon him) was sent to the people of 'Ad to call them to worship God alone (7:65).

q: The she-camel given as a sign to the people of Thamud is linked to which prophet (peace be upon him)?
explain: Salih (peace be upon him) was sent to Thamud, and the she-camel was a sign from God for them (7:73).

q: Which prophet (peace be upon him) was thrown into a fire by his people, and God made it cool and safe for him?
explain: When his people threw Ibrahim (peace be upon him) into the fire, God ordered it to be coolness and safety for him (21:68-69).

q: According to the Qur'an, which prophet (peace be upon him) understood the words of an ant warning the other ants?
explain: Sulayman (peace be upon him) heard an ant warn the others as his army came near, and he smiled and thanked God (27:18-19).

q: Which prophet (peace be upon him) was the father of Yahya (John)?
explain: Zakariyya (peace be upon him) prayed for a child in his old age and was given the good news of Yahya (19:7).

q: In which city was the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ born?
explain: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born in Mecca, in the tribe of Quraysh.

q: Where did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ receive the first revelation?
explain: The first revelation came in the cave of Hira, on the Mountain of Light near Mecca, where he used to retreat.

q: Which angel brought the revelation to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
explain: The angel Jibril (peace be upon him) brought the Qur'an to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

q: What was the first word of the Qur'an revealed to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
explain: The first revelation begins with the word 'Iqra', meaning read or recite (96:1).

q: Who was the first wife of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
explain: Khadija, a respected merchant of Mecca, was his first wife. He married no other woman while she was alive.

q: In which year of the common era did the Hijra, the migration from Mecca to Medina, take place?
explain: The Hijra took place in 622 CE. That year later became year 1 of the Islamic calendar.

q: What was the city of Medina called before the Hijra?
explain: The city was called Yathrib. After the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ settled there it became known as Medina, 'the City'.

q: In which cave did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ take shelter during the Hijra?
explain: He hid in the cave of Thawr with his companion Abu Bakr while Quraysh searched for them. The Qur'an mentions this moment in 9:40.

q: In which year of the Hijra did the Battle of Badr take place?
explain: The Battle of Badr took place in Ramadan of the year 2 AH. It was the first major battle of the Muslims.

q: What was the name of the grandfather who took care of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ after his mother died?
explain: His grandfather Abd al-Muttalib, a leader of Mecca, looked after him. After the grandfather's death, his uncle Abu Talib took him in.

q: What was the name of the mother of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
explain: His mother was Amina bint Wahb. She died when he was still a small child. Halima as-Sa'diyya was his wet nurse.

q: To which tribe did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ belong?
explain: He belonged to Quraysh, the tribe of Mecca, in the clan of Banu Hashim.

q: What is the name of the truce agreed between the Muslims and Quraysh in the year 6 AH?
options: The Pact of the Virtuous (Hilf al-Fudul)
explain: The Treaty of Hudaybiyya was agreed in 6 AH near Mecca. It brought a period of peace during which Islam spread widely.

q: In which year of the Hijra did the Conquest of Mecca take place?
explain: The Muslims entered Mecca in the year 8 AH (630 CE). The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ forgave its people.

q: Before prophethood, what nickname did the people of Mecca give to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
explain: He was known as al-Amin, the Trustworthy, because of his honesty. People left their valuables in his care.

q: Who was the first muezzin of Islam?
explain: Bilal ibn Rabah, a freed slave of Abyssinian origin, was chosen by the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to call the adhan.

q: Which companion travelled with the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ during the Hijra?
explain: Abu Bakr was his companion on the journey from Mecca to Medina and stayed with him in the cave of Thawr.

q: Which companion suggested digging a trench to defend Medina?
explain: Salman al-Farisi, who came from Persia, suggested the trench. This is why the battle of 5 AH is called the Battle of the Trench.

q: Which companion is known by the title 'Sword of God' (Sayf Allah)?
explain: Khalid ibn al-Walid, a famous commander, is known as Sayf Allah, the Sword of God.

q: Who was the first person to believe in the message of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
explain: His wife Khadija was the first to believe in him. She comforted and supported him from the very first revelation.

q: Under which caliph was the Hijri calendar adopted, with the year of the Hijra as its starting point?
explain: The Hijri calendar was set up during the caliphate of Umar ibn al-Khattab, a few years after the death of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

q: Which companion, a scribe of the revelation, was given the task of gathering the Qur'an into one written collection?
explain: Zayd ibn Thabit, one of the scribes of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, gathered the written Qur'an into one collection during the caliphate of Abu Bakr.

q: Which companion was sent to Yathrib before the Hijra to teach Islam to its people?
explain: Mus'ab ibn Umayr was sent to Yathrib after the first pledge of Aqaba. Many of its people accepted Islam through him.

q: In which battle was Hamza, the uncle of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, killed?
explain: Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib fell as a martyr at the Battle of Uhud, in the year 3 AH.

q: Who is remembered as the first martyr of Islam?
explain: Sumayya bint Khayyat, the mother of Ammar ibn Yasir, was killed in Mecca for refusing to give up her faith.

q: Which companion spoke for the Muslim emigrants before the Negus, the king of Abyssinia?
explain: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib explained Islam to the Negus, who then let the Muslims live in safety in his land.

q: Which daughter of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ married Ali ibn Abi Talib?
explain: Fatima married Ali ibn Abi Talib in Medina. They were the parents of al-Hasan and al-Husayn.

q: What name is given to the people of Medina who welcomed and helped the emigrants from Mecca?
explain: The Muslims of Medina are called the Ansar, the Helpers. Those who emigrated from Mecca are called the Muhajirun.

q: Who slept in the bed of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ on the night he left Mecca for the Hijra?
explain: The young Ali ibn Abi Talib took his place in the bed that night and stayed behind to return the goods people had entrusted to him.

q: In whose house did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ live in Medina while his mosque was being built?
explain: He stayed in the house of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari until his mosque and his rooms were built.

q: How many surahs does the Qur'an contain?
explain: The Qur'an has 114 surahs, from al-Fatiha to an-Nas.

q: Which is the longest surah of the Qur'an?
explain: Al-Baqara, the 2nd surah, is the longest in the Qur'an.

q: Which is the shortest surah of the Qur'an?
explain: Al-Kawthar, the 108th surah, is the shortest: it has only three short verses.

q: Which surah opens the Qur'an?
explain: Al-Fatiha, 'the Opening', is the first surah of the Qur'an and is recited in every prayer.

q: Which surah is placed last in the Qur'an?
explain: An-Nas, the 114th surah, closes the Qur'an.

q: Into how many parts (juz') is the Qur'an divided?
explain: The Qur'an is divided into 30 juz', which makes it easy to read it all in one month.

q: In which month did the revelation of the Qur'an begin?
explain: The Qur'an says that it was sent down in the month of Ramadan (2:185).

q: In which surah is Ayat al-Kursi, the Verse of the Throne, found?
explain: Ayat al-Kursi is verse 255 of Surah al-Baqara (2:255).

q: Which is the only surah that does not begin with the basmala?
explain: At-Tawba, the 9th surah, is the only one that does not open with 'In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful'.

q: In which surah does the basmala appear twice?
explain: In Surah an-Naml the basmala comes at the opening and again in the letter of Sulayman, peace be upon him (27:30).

q: Which surah of the Qur'an bears the name of the mother of Isa (peace be upon him)?
explain: The 19th surah is named after Maryam, the mother of Isa (peace be upon them). She is the only woman mentioned by name in the Qur'an.

q: Over about how many years was the Qur'an revealed?
explain: The Qur'an was revealed little by little over about 23 years, first in Mecca and then in Medina.

q: How many verses does Surah al-Fatiha have?
explain: Al-Fatiha has seven verses. It is recited in every unit of the prayer.

q: What are the surahs revealed before the Hijra called?
explain: Surahs revealed before the Hijra are called Meccan, and those revealed after it are called Medinan.

q: Which is the longest verse of the Qur'an?
explain: The longest verse is verse 282 of al-Baqara. It teaches people to write down their debts and to call witnesses.

q: Which city was the capital of the Umayyad caliphate?
explain: The Umayyads ruled from Damascus, in Syria, from 661 to 750.

q: Which Abbasid caliph founded the city of Baghdad in 762?
explain: Caliph al-Mansur founded Baghdad in 762 on the banks of the Tigris. It became one of the greatest cities in the world.

q: Who captured and destroyed Baghdad in 1258?
explain: The Mongol army led by Hulagu took Baghdad in 1258, which ended the Abbasid caliphate of Baghdad.

q: Which Ottoman sultan took Constantinople in 1453?
explain: Mehmed II, known as 'the Conqueror', took Constantinople in 1453. The city became the Ottoman capital, Istanbul.

q: Who led the Muslim army that crossed from North Africa into the Iberian Peninsula in 711?
explain: Tariq ibn Ziyad crossed the strait in 711. The rock of Gibraltar is named after him: Jabal Tariq, 'the mountain of Tariq'.

q: Who took Jerusalem back from the Crusaders in 1187?
explain: Salah ad-Din al-Ayyubi retook Jerusalem in 1187, after his victory at the Battle of Hattin.

q: Which city, the last Muslim kingdom of al-Andalus, fell in 1492?
explain: The Nasrid kingdom of Granada fell in 1492, ending almost eight centuries of Muslim rule in parts of the Iberian Peninsula.

q: Who defeated the Mongols at the Battle of Ain Jalut in 1260?
explain: The Mamluks of Egypt stopped the Mongol advance at Ain Jalut, in Palestine, in 1260.

q: Which dynasty took over the caliphate in 750 and later made Baghdad its capital?
explain: The Abbasids replaced the Umayyads in 750 and founded Baghdad in 762.

q: Which Umayyad prince fled to al-Andalus and founded the emirate of Cordoba in 756?
explain: Abd al-Rahman I, a survivor of the Umayyad family, reached al-Andalus and founded the emirate of Cordoba in 756.

q: The Ottoman dynasty takes its name from its founder. Who was he?
explain: Osman I founded the Ottoman state in Anatolia around 1300. The word 'Ottoman' comes from his name.

q: Who founded the Mughal Empire in India in 1526?
explain: Babur founded the Mughal Empire after his victory at the Battle of Panipat in 1526.

q: Which 16th-century Ottoman sultan is known as 'the Magnificent' and 'the Lawgiver'?
explain: Suleiman I ruled from 1520 to 1566, when the Ottoman Empire was at its height. He is called 'Kanuni', the Lawgiver.

q: Mansa Musa, famous for his pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324, ruled which empire?
explain: Mansa Musa ruled the Mali Empire in West Africa. His pilgrimage of 1324 made the wealth of Mali famous far and wide.

q: Which Seljuk sultan won the Battle of Manzikert against the Byzantines in 1071?
explain: Alp Arslan defeated the Byzantine army at Manzikert in 1071, which opened Anatolia to the Turks.

q: Which branch of mathematics takes its name from the book 'al-Jabr' by al-Khwarizmi?
explain: The word algebra comes from 'al-jabr', in the title of the book that al-Khwarizmi wrote in Baghdad in the 9th century.

q: The word 'algorithm' comes from the Latin form of which scholar's name?
explain: 'Algorithm' comes from 'Algoritmi', the Latin form of the name of the mathematician al-Khwarizmi.

q: Who wrote the 'Canon of Medicine' (al-Qanun fi al-Tibb)?
explain: Ibn Sina wrote the Canon of Medicine in the 11th century. It was used to teach medicine for centuries, in the Muslim world and in Europe.

q: Which scholar wrote the 'Book of Optics' and explained that we see because light enters the eye?
explain: Ibn al-Haytham, who lived in the 10th and 11th centuries, wrote the Book of Optics (Kitab al-Manazir) and relied on careful experiments.

q: The Andalusian scholar al-Zahrawi is famous as a pioneer in which field?
explain: Al-Zahrawi, who lived near Cordoba in the 10th century, described surgical operations and many instruments in his encyclopedia al-Tasrif.

q: Which physician wrote a famous treatise that told smallpox apart from measles?
explain: Al-Razi, a great physician of the 9th and 10th centuries, wrote a treatise on smallpox and measles that carefully describes both illnesses.

q: Which 13th-century physician described how blood passes from the heart through the lungs?
explain: Ibn al-Nafis described the pulmonary circulation of the blood in the 13th century, long before it was known in Europe.

q: Which 11th-century scholar calculated the radius of the Earth and wrote a major study of India?
explain: Al-Biruni measured the radius of the Earth with remarkable accuracy and wrote a detailed book about India.

q: Which geographer drew a famous map of the world for King Roger II of Sicily in the 12th century?
explain: Al-Idrisi completed his map of the world and the book that goes with it in 1154, at the court of Roger II in Sicily.

q: Jabir ibn Hayyan is especially known for his work in which field?
explain: Jabir ibn Hayyan is one of the great names of early chemistry (alchemy), with many works attributed to him.

q: In which city was the House of Wisdom (Bayt al-Hikma), a great centre of translation and learning?
explain: The House of Wisdom flourished in Abbasid Baghdad, where scholars translated and studied works from Greek, Persian and Indian traditions.

q: Who wrote the 'Muqaddima', a famous work on history and society?
explain: Ibn Khaldun, born in Tunis in 1332, wrote the Muqaddima. He is seen as a forerunner of sociology and of the modern study of history.

q: What was the astrolabe, an instrument perfected by Muslim scholars, used for?
options: Observing the position of the sun and stars
explain: The astrolabe was used to observe the sun and stars, which helped people tell the time and find directions.

q: What is the engineer al-Jazari, who finished his famous book in 1206, known for?
explain: Al-Jazari wrote the Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices, which describes water clocks, pumps and automata.

q: By what Latin name is the Andalusian scholar Ibn Rushd known in Europe?
explain: Ibn Rushd of Cordoba is known as Averroes. His commentaries on Aristotle were read widely in medieval Europe.

q: How many pillars does Islam have?
explain: Islam has five pillars: the testimony of faith, prayer, zakat, fasting in Ramadan and the pilgrimage to Mecca.

q: What is the first pillar of Islam?
explain: The first pillar is the shahada: to bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad ﷺ is His Messenger.

q: How many obligatory prayers are there each day?
explain: There are five obligatory prayers each day: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha.

q: What is the name of the dawn prayer?
explain: Fajr is the dawn prayer, the first of the five daily prayers.

q: How many obligatory units (rak'at) does the Fajr prayer have?
explain: The obligatory Fajr prayer has two rak'at.

q: Which month of the Islamic calendar is Ramadan?
explain: Ramadan is the ninth month of the Hijri calendar. It is the month of fasting.

q: In Ramadan, when does each day's fast begin?
explain: The fast begins at dawn, when the first light appears, as the Qur'an explains in 2:187.

q: What is the meal that breaks the fast in the evening called?
explain: Iftar is the meal that breaks the fast. Suhur is the meal taken before dawn.

q: What is the usual rate of zakat on savings such as money, gold and silver?
explain: Zakat on savings is 2.5%, one fortieth, once the minimum amount has been held for a full lunar year.

q: In which month does the Hajj take place?
explain: The Hajj takes place in Dhul-Hijja, the twelfth and last month of the Hijri calendar.

q: How many times do pilgrims go around the Kaaba in one tawaf?
explain: A tawaf is made of seven circuits around the Kaaba.

q: Between which two hills do pilgrims walk during the sa'i?
explain: Pilgrims walk seven times between Safa and Marwa, which the Qur'an calls symbols of God (2:158).

q: On which day of Dhul-Hijja do pilgrims stand at Arafat?
explain: The standing at Arafat is on the 9th of Dhul-Hijja. It is the heart of the Hajj.

q: How many times in a lifetime is the Hajj required of a Muslim who is able to make it?
explain: The Hajj is required once in a lifetime for those who are able to make the journey (3:97).

q: Towards which city did the first Muslims pray before the qibla became the Kaaba?
explain: The first Muslims prayed towards Jerusalem. The qibla was then turned towards the Sacred Mosque in Mecca (2:144).

q: Who founded the mosque of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez in the 9th century, which grew into a famous university?
explain: Fatima al-Fihri founded al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, Morocco, in 859. It is often described as the oldest university still in activity.

q: In which city of al-Andalus is the great mosque famous for its forest of columns and its red and white arches?
explain: The Great Mosque of Cordoba was begun in the 8th century, when Cordoba was the capital of al-Andalus.

q: In which city is the Alhambra palace?
explain: The Alhambra stands in Granada, in the south of Spain. It was the palace of the Nasrid rulers.

q: Which Mughal emperor had the Taj Mahal built?
explain: Shah Jahan had the Taj Mahal built in Agra in the 17th century, in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

q: In which city was the great traveller Ibn Battuta born?
explain: Ibn Battuta was born in Tangier, Morocco, in 1304. He travelled for nearly thirty years across Africa, Asia and Europe.

q: Timbuktu, a famous centre of learning and manuscripts, is in which present-day country?
explain: Timbuktu is in Mali. Its mosques and schools drew students and scholars from across West Africa.

q: In which city is al-Azhar, one of the oldest universities in the world?
explain: Al-Azhar was founded in Cairo in the 10th century and is still a major centre of learning today.

q: In which city is the Dome of the Rock?
explain: The Dome of the Rock is in Jerusalem. It was completed at the end of the 7th century under the Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik.

q: Which Ottoman architect designed the Süleymaniye Mosque in Istanbul?
explain: Mimar Sinan, chief architect of the Ottoman Empire in the 16th century, designed the Süleymaniye in Istanbul and the Selimiye in Edirne.

q: In the medieval Muslim world, what was a 'bimaristan'?
explain: A bimaristan was a hospital. Cities such as Baghdad, Damascus and Cairo had large hospitals where the sick were treated.

q: What is the first month of the Hijri calendar?
explain: Muharram is the first of the twelve months of the Hijri calendar, which follows the moon.

q: In a mosque, what is the mihrab?
options: The pulpit used for the Friday sermon
The niche that shows the direction of Mecca
The tower used for the call to prayer
explain: The mihrab is a niche in the wall that shows the qibla, the direction of Mecca. The pulpit is called the minbar and the tower the minaret.

q: The Great Mosque of Kairouan, one of the oldest in Africa, is in which country?
explain: Kairouan is in Tunisia. Its Great Mosque goes back to the founding of the city by Uqba ibn Nafi in 670.

q: The Kufic script, one of the oldest styles of Arabic calligraphy, is named after which city?
explain: Kufic script takes its name from Kufa, in Iraq. Many early copies of the Qur'an were written in this angular style.

q: In Islamic civilisation, what is a 'waqf'?
explain: A waqf is property set aside for good, such as a school, a hospital or a fountain. Its income keeps serving people over time.
